items.title: Spectral Memory of an Evolving Localization Length — Quantum Coherence, Clock Reconstruction and Intergalactic Constraints
items.summary: Abstract Can an evolving localization length leave a mechanical record from which its history can be reconstructed? We study a completely positive momentum-transfer channel in which a single geometric aperture controls both the event rate and the transfer width. On the constant-winding area branch, the accumulated radial spectrum develops an inverse-cubic reference tail whose amplitude uniquely determines the coefficient of the associated logarithmically enhanced quadratic coherence law. A Gaussian finite-size response closes the channel exactly: the coherent event count generates all even transfer moments, while a single derivative determines both the small-separation coherence curvature…

items.title: Equivariant First-Jet Torsion Sources for an SU (2)/ U (1) Director
items.summary: Let the fundamental field be a pair (ϕ, Q), where ϕ is a real scalar and Q is a unit imaginary-quaternion director, equivalently a section of an associated S² ≃ SU(2)/U(1) bundle; write Ψ = ϕQ only as composite notation. We determine the module of local torsion sources that are homogeneous and linear in j¹(ϕ, Q), Lorentz equivariant, and internally SU(2) gauge invariant. Two independent mechanisms control the answer: Lorentz intertwiners classify the amplitude covector, while isotropy-fixed covectors test the director derivative. items.title: Stochastic Mass–Energy Interconversion and Observational Constraints: Matter-Wave Interferometry, Cosmic Expansion, and Emergent Gravity
items.summary: Spontaneous subatomic mass–energy interconversion has been proposed as a microscopic stochastic process connecting quantum coherence with effective gravitational dynamics. I reconstruct the hypothesis as restricted mathematical models and confront it with published interferometric and cosmological measurements rather than presuming its empirical success. Gaussian differential mass noise yields a correlation-dependent attenuation of two-path fringe visibility; perfectly common-mode noise cancels. Published molecular interferometry extending beyond 25,000 Da reports selected fringe visibilities exceeding 90% of the quantum-theory expectation. Under explicit simplifying assumptions this…

items.title: Interfacial Polarization Dynamics of Nitrile Dipoles in Organic Synaptic Transistors for Acoustic Reservoir Computing.
items.summary: Polar polymer interlayers have emerged as core functional layers in organic synaptic transistors (OSTs), enabling diverse neuromorphic behaviors through interfacial dipolar polarization and relaxation. However, the interfacial dipolar mechanisms governing memory window (ΔV) formation and modulation remain insufficiently understood. Here, polyacrylonitrile (PAN) is selected as a representative polar polymer interlayer to exploit nitrile (CN) dipolar relaxation for temporal acoustic reservoir computing (RC). It is found that the ΔV varies nonmonotonically with PAN concentration, suggesting a dipolar competition mechanism between interfacial polarization strength and dipole relaxation…

items.title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In 2 Se 3 for ferroelectric homojunctions.
items.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric semiconductors offer unique opportunities for ultrathin non-volatile memory and neuromorphic devices, yet the role of stacking order in intrinsic ferroelectric systems remains largely unexplored. Here we report the stacking-controlled growth of large-area 2D β'- and α-In 2 Se 3 with distinct 2H and 3R configurations through chemical vapour deposition by regulating selenium kinetics and strain relaxation. By combining atomic-resolution microscopy, non-linear optical characterization and first-principles calculations, we uncover a strong correlation between stacking order and ferroelectric behaviour: β'-In 2 Se 3 undergoes an…

items.title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing.
items.summary: Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer…

items.title: Bias-Switchable ZnO/AlScN Heterojunction for Self-Powered UV Photodetection and Neuromorphic Learning.
items.summary: The convergence of ultraviolet (UV) communication and neuromorphic computing demands multifunctional devices that integrate high-speed photodetection with synaptic learning, yet the intrinsic mismatch between fast photoresponse and slow memory retention poses a fundamental challenge for monolithic integration. Here, we report a dual-mode UV optoelectronic device based on a ZnO/AlScN heterojunction, in which flexible switching between a self-powered photodetection mode and a neuromorphic mode is achieved through bias modulation. In mode I, operating at zero bias, the device exploits the type-II band alignment and built-in electric field of the heterojunction to realize a rapid response to…

items.title: Emergence Requires No Miracle: The Eligibility Trace as the Necessary Engine of Reward-Driven Differentiation in Spiking Networks
items.summary: Abstract Emergent differentiation in reward-driven learning requires local events to persist long enough for global evaluation to bind them. In a spiking neural network trained with reward-modulated STDP (N = 800-80,000 neurons, up to 128M synapses), five-condition ablation shows that removing the eligibility trace eliminates positive sparsification at every scale on the post-warmup baseline (Delta Gini = -0.006 +/- 0.001 at N=800; -0.005 +/- 0.003 at N=80,000); measured from random initialization, the traceless condition still drifts upward at small scale (+0.088 at N=800), so we state the necessity claim on the post-warmup baseline and report both baselines. items.title: Fully analog end-to-end online training with real-time adaptability in integrated photonics
items.summary: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware is emerging as a transformative platform for artificial intelligence and machine learning, offering unprecedented computational speed and energy efficiency. Although several analog neuromorphic photonic systems have been demonstrated in recent years, state-of-the-art architectures still face key challenges, particularly in achieving real-time online training with high-speed signals, fully on-chip end-to-end analog implementation, online tracking, and adaptive learning under dynamic environmental conditions. Here, we demonstrate the first hardware realization of an on-chip photonic multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) algorithm that performs in-situ, on-the-fly…

items.title: Spiking Neural Networks for Image Classification and Recognition
items.summary: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute the third generation of neural computational models, replacing the continuous-valued activations of conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) with discrete, asynchronous spike events that more closely resemble the dynamics of biological neurons. By encoding information in the timing and sparsity of spikes, SNNs promise substantial reductions in energy consumption when deployed on event-driven neuromorphic hardware, making them attractive for image classification and recognition on resource-constrained platforms. This paper presents a deep SNN image classifier built from leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons and trained end to end with…

items.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Feral AI and the Emergence of Digital Ecosystems
items.summary: The digital world is approaching a profound phase transition, whose primary drivers, we argue, are different from those that dominate current discussions of AI risk. The transition need not begin with a superintelligent system escaping human control, or with an AI acquiring the ability and motivation to reproduce. Rather, we suggest that it may get under way as AI agents routinely delegate tasks by creating or recruiting other agents. As delegation becomes widespread and recursive, vast numbers of agents will be created; inevitably, some will persist, spread, and create others beyond their original tasks and environments. At scale, this changes the rules of the game. Digital environments…

items.title: Civilizational Unbinding Transition and the Demise of Human Warfare in the Superintelligence (SI) Society
items.summary: Abstract For millennia, large-scale inter-group violent conflict has been treated as an ineradicable structural feature of human civilization, with war mortality assumed to only follow a gradual, asymptotic downward trajectory. This study introduces the ‌Civilizational Unbinding Index (U)‌, a quantifiable framework that measures the progressive relaxation of natural, social and survival constraints across 10,000 years of human history, validated against the fully open Seshat Global History Databank. Through 1,000 independent multi-agent evolutionary simulations, we robustly demonstrate a statistically significant negative correlation between the Unbinding Index U and annual war mortality…

items.title: The Dirac Equation and the Two-Photon Model of the Electron: A Clifford-Algebra Construction within the Delta-c Mechanics Framework
items.summary: In a previous paper, “The Electron as a Composition of Two Vacuum-Polarization-Confined Photons,” an electron model was developed in which two counter-propagating phase-conjugate photons are bound in orbit by the self-induced gradient in the speed of light arising from their mutual vacuum polarization. The model accounts for rest mass and spin, proposes a mechanism for charge, and has no singularity and no negative-energy solutions. The present paper focuses on the mathematical structure of that bound state. items.title: PrepNet: A Multi-Task Geometric Deep Learning Framework for Automatic Detection and Numbering of Prepared Tooth in 3D Dental Scan Models.
items.summary: Objectives This study aimed to develop and evaluate PrepNet, a multi-task geometric deep learning framework, for automatic detection and numbering of the prepared tooth in 3D dental scan models (DSMs). Methods In this study, we propose PrepNet, a multi-task geometric deep learning framework designed to simultaneously predict the target ROI centroid, estimate the ROI size, and classify the tooth number from 3D DSMs. PrepNet integrates local graph feature extraction using DGCNN to capture surface variations with global contextual modeling via a Point Cloud Transformer to encode long-range dental structures. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Language-model systems now rewrite their own memory, code, and weights, and small language models now run on phones and embedded boards. This paper asks whether the two developments have met: can a system improve itself within the memory, energy, thermal, latency, and connectivity budgets of a device? We define edge self-improvement as a verified update loop under a timevarying device budget, and we classify 63 works along three axes: the improved component, where computation ran in the reported evaluation, and the verification tier. items.summary: As an emergent field stimulated by insights from the biological, chemical, physical, and quantum sciences, quantum biology explores how quantum phenomena such as superradiance, tunneling, and entanglement can be leveraged to enhance, influence, and probe biological processes across a diversity of scales and physical degrees of freedom. This review surveys key theoretical, computational, and experimental developments over the last decade, providing relevant historical background and scientific context going back as far as Bohr's 1932 lecture on "Light and Life" in Copenhagen. items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. Here we introduce a bipartite extension of the nPSO model called nBPSO, motivated by the prevalence of community organization in real-world bipartite networks and the emerging evidence of hyperbolic hierarchical connectivity in trained sparse neural networks. nBPSO provides explicit control over link density, degree distribution, average clustering, and community organization. items.title: Experimental platform to study the neuronal mechanisms of magnetoreception in the honey bee.
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) offer an alternative model for investigating magnetoreception, exhibiting reliable navigation and behavioral responses to magnetic fields. Thanks to their compact brains, well-matched to the penetration depth of modern optical imaging techniques, they may offer insights into the neural and biochemical mechanisms underlying this sense, something that standard models, like migrating birds, have not so far provided. But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. The approach, presented here, bridges quantum biology and neuroscience, aiming at testing the…

items.title: Toward quantum-informed addiction medicine: Coherence, entangled-photon imaging, and a theranostic hypothesis.
items.summary: Background Quantum biology has shown that selected biological processes depend on quantum effects, including coherence, tunnelling, and spin-dependent reactions. In parallel, quantum imaging now uses entangled photons to extract biological information at low photon flux. Early evidence that biological tissue can alter photon entanglement in disease-associated ways raises a translational question: whether decoherence itself can become a diagnostic signal. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.
items.summary: Human conscious thought often appears as a diffuse, unstable, and only partly verbalizable field until attention, questioning, decision, or speech stabilizes it into a reportable form. This manuscript develops a quantum-inspired neural framework for that transition. The proposal does not claim that consciousness literally depends on microscopic quantum computation, that the brain implements a physical quantum computer, or that neuronal tissue maintains macroscopic quantum coherence.
